```python
def rearrange_bigger(n):
    """Return the next bigger number formed by rearranging n's digits, or False if none exists."""
    digits = list(str(n))
    i = len(digits) - 2
    while i >= 0 and digits[i] >= digits[i + 1]:
        i -= 1
    if i < 0:
        return False
    j = len(digits) - 1
    while digits[j] <= digits[i]:
        j -= 1
    digits[i], digits[j] = digits[j], digits[i]
    digits[i + 1:] = sorted(digits[i + 1:])
    return int(''.join(digits))
```

I changed the no-solution return from `None` to `False` to match the team note. Both are falsy, so `assert rearrange_bigger(12) == 21` still passes. The suffix is now sorted explicitly instead of reversed. The suffix is always non-increasing at that point, so the two give the same result.
